title: What's New: Smarter Pipelines (2025 release wave 2)

chapters.title: Introduction and overview of pipeline challenges
The problem: managing versions across 200+ app.json files
Live demo: using props files with multiple projects
How props files work with ALC and Visual Studio Code
Introducing dotnet tool installation for command line tools
Live demo: using AL command line tool across platforms

features.name: directory.app.props.json file
features.description: A new file format inspired by MS build props file that centralizes application settings across multiple AL projects. It contains a variables section for declaring reusable values and a properties section that map to app.json properties.
caveats: Properties are expanded during package creation, not at load time for VS Code editing
Changes to props file require VS Code reload to take effect in editor
Only specific properties currently supported, with possibility of adding more

features.name: AL command line tool via dotnet tools
features.description: A new way to install and access AL command line tools using the dotnet tool package mechanism. Provides a simpler, cross-platform method for getting access to command line tools in pipelines.
caveats: Only one alias can be added via dotnet tools, so AL alias points to AL tool with all toolchain commands
Naming convention may change before release (uppercase ALT may be lowercased)

features.name: Variable substitution in app.json
features.description: Allows using placeholder syntax like $(version) in app.json files which are replaced with values from directory.app.props.json during build time.
caveats: Placeholders require values from props file; missing values cause build errors

features.name: Property override in individual projects
features.description: Individual app.json files can override properties from directory.app.props.json by including them locally, allowing project-specific customization while still leveraging centralized defaults.

features.name: AL tool with subcommands
features.description: The AL command line tool now supports multiple subcommands accessed via 'al compile', 'al help', 'al get-application-manifest' and similar, consolidating multiple tools under a single AL tool entrypoint.

features.name: AL-Go integration planned
features.description: Future plans to integrate the directory.app.props.json and dotnet tools features into AL-Go for GitHub, providing this functionality to users of that automation framework.
caveats: Timeline is unspecified ('soon or in the future')
